body:
`run_preflight()` in scripts/autopilot-tick.sh pipes preflight through
`tee "$PREFLIGHT_LAST"` (state/preflight-last.txt). That file is rewritten on
EVERY run, pass or fail, so the moment a later tick's preflight succeeds the
failing run's output is gone.

OBSERVED 2026-08-09: preflight failed rc=1 at 04:00:05Z after 5m53s. By 04:21
the file read "== preflight OK ==". The only surviving record of the failure is
two lines in autopilot-tick.log saying rc=1 with no reason, plus a
`tick-preflight-failed` ledger row that says "see state/autopilot-tick.log" —
which does not contain the reason either.

The 5m53s duration is the tell: the autopilot test suite (step 5/5) takes ~4.5
min and every other step is seconds, so the failure was almost certainly a flaky
test. Which test is unknowable now, which is the whole problem — a flaky gate
that wedges the tick is exactly the thing that needs a name.

Compounding it: the ntfy page built for a red-preflight streak interpolates
`${PREFLIGHT_RED:-see state/preflight-last.txt}`, pointing the operator at the
file that self-erases. By the time a human reads the page the evidence can
already be overwritten by a passing run.

Fix shape: write failures to a non-clobbering path — state/preflight-fail-<TS>.txt
— and keep preflight-last.txt as the rolling copy. Retain the last few, and have
the ledger row and the ntfy text name the retained file rather than the log.
title: Preflight failure diagnostics are overwritten by the next successful tick
